lessons.title: Ways to Load Data into Oracle Fusion

slots.practicalActivity: For LTV Manufacturing Corporation, build a one-page comparison table of the four doors into Oracle Fusion data -- manual entry, FBDI, ADFdi, and REST API integration -- and for each one write the row-volume and frequency it fits best, using the lesson's own three-question framework (how many rows, how often, who's doing the work).
slots.deliverable: A four-row decision table (manual entry / FBDI / ADFdi / REST API) with volume and frequency notes for each, ready to reuse for every scenario later in the course.

lessons.title: The FBDI Process: Template to Import
Universal Content Management and Import Locations

slots.practicalActivity: Draw the full eight-step FBDI pipeline from memory (download, populate, generate CSV, zip, upload to UCM, Load Interface File for Import, product-specific import, review results), marking exactly where the 'staging boundary' sits. Then open File Import and Export in your practice environment and locate the account used for Supplier/Procurement imports versus the one used for General Ledger imports, confirming they are genuinely separate.
slots.deliverable: A hand-drawn eight-step pipeline diagram with the staging boundary marked, plus a short note identifying two different UCM import-account names you located.

slots.practicalActivity: Download the real Supplier Import FBDI template for LTV Manufacturing Corporation from the File-Based Data Import spreadsheets page, open its Instructions tab, and identify which columns on the data tab are required versus optional and which are coded lookups rather than free text. Enter 5 sample supplier rows, deliberately using a friendly label (like 'US Dollars') instead of a currency code in one row so you can see the mistake before it causes a rejection later.
slots.deliverable: A downloaded Supplier Import template with 5 populated rows, one intentionally containing a label-instead-of-code error you've documented for yourself.

slots.practicalActivity: Fix the currency-code error from the previous slot, delete any leftover sample rows below your real data, then use the template's Instructions-tab macro to generate the CSV file(s) and zip them into one file, confirming the zip's internal structure matches the pattern shown in the lesson (one CSV per worksheet, e.g. SUPPLIER and SITE).
slots.deliverable: One corrected, clean 5-row Supplier Import template with its generated CSV file(s) zipped into a single upload-ready .zip.

slots.practicalActivity: Take your zipped Supplier Import file from the previous slot and run it all the way through the pipeline for LTV Manufacturing Corporation: upload to File Import and Export, run Load Interface File for Import, then run the Supplier Import process. Review the execution report to see how many of your 5 suppliers succeeded versus were rejected, and why.
slots.deliverable: A completed Supplier Import run with its execution report, documenting the final success/rejection count for your 5 supplier rows.

lessons.title: Uploading Files and Loading to Interface Tables

slots.practicalActivity: Build a second, larger Supplier Import batch (15 rows) for LTV Manufacturing Corporation, upload it, and submit Load Interface File for Import followed by the product-specific import process. While both are running, open Scheduled Processes, expand the parent Load Interface File for Import row to find its child processes, and track each submission from Pending through Running to Succeeded, Warning, or Error.
slots.deliverable: A documented Scheduled Processes trace for one full submission, showing the parent process, at least one expanded child process, and the final status of each.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the execution report for your 15-row supplier batch and read its row-level detail: which rows succeeded, which were rejected, and the stated reason for each rejection. Then query the supplier interface tables directly to find any rows still sitting there after the import process ran, and explain in your own words why a row can remain staged instead of becoming a live record.
slots.deliverable: A row-by-row reading of one execution report plus a short written explanation of any rows still found sitting in the interface tables afterward.

slots.practicalActivity: Download the Journal Import template, populate GL_INTERFACE with 8 journal lines for LTV Manufacturing Corporation that individually look valid but whose debits and credits do not net to zero as a batch. Run the full pipeline through Import Journals and confirm the entire batch is rejected as a group for the imbalance -- the one General Ledger rule the lesson says is never relaxed -- then fix the amounts and rerun until it imports cleanly.
slots.deliverable: One Journal Import run that failed on a documented debits-credits imbalance, followed by a corrected run that succeeded and created real journal entries.

slots.practicalActivity: Download the Payables Open Interface Import template and populate it with 6 supplier invoices for LTV Manufacturing Corporation, including header and line detail, deliberately reusing one invoice number already used by an existing supplier so one row will be rejected as a duplicate. Run Import Payables Invoices and confirm the 5 clean rows create real invoices while the duplicate is rejected with a clear reason.
slots.deliverable: One Payables Invoice Import run creating 5 real invoices plus one documented duplicate-invoice-number rejection.

slots.practicalActivity: Populate the AutoInvoice interface template with 6 customer transaction lines for LTV Manufacturing Corporation representing invoices originating from an external order system, then run AutoInvoice Import and review its execution report, noting which validation rules (transaction type, customer, transaction source) apply uniquely to receivables versus the rules you already saw on journals and payables.
slots.deliverable: One completed AutoInvoice Import run with an execution report, plus a short comparison note on receivables-specific validation versus journals and payables.

slots.practicalActivity: Populate the Mass Additions Create interface template with 5 fixed-asset additions for LTV Manufacturing Corporation (description, cost, category, in-service date), run the import, and then review the Prepare Mass Additions page to confirm each row landed as a ready-to-post asset line before it becomes a depreciating asset.
slots.deliverable: One Mass Additions Create run producing 5 reviewable asset lines in Prepare Mass Additions.

slots.practicalActivity: Populate the Bank Statement Import template with a 10-line statement for LTV Manufacturing Corporation's operating account, including both matched and unmatched transaction lines, run the import, and confirm the statement loads for Cash Management reconciliation -- noting why, unlike every other module this chapter, this is a feed that is never a manual or ADFdi candidate.
slots.deliverable: One imported bank statement with 10 lines ready for reconciliation, plus a one-sentence note on why bank statements are FBDI-only.

slots.practicalActivity: Take the Payables Invoice batch from earlier in the chapter and, using Correct Import Errors, open the rejected duplicate-invoice-number row in its connected spreadsheet, change the invoice number, and resubmit only that one corrected row -- never the whole original file -- to avoid re-processing the 5 rows that already succeeded.
slots.deliverable: One row fixed and resubmitted through Correct Import Errors, with the original 5 successful invoices left untouched and confirmed still correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: confirm every row from this chapter's Payables batch has either succeeded or been resolved, then purge the stale rejected interface rows for that batch. Afterward, without new instruction, diagnose and resolve three fresh planted failures across three different modules (a journal imbalance, a payables duplicate, and an AutoInvoice validation error) end to end: identify the cause, fix only the affected rows, resubmit, and confirm success.
slots.deliverable: One documented interface-data purge, plus three independently diagnosed-and-resolved import failures across journals, payables, and receivables.

slots.practicalActivity: Install the ADFdi add-in and launch Create Journal in Spreadsheet from the Journals work area for LTV Manufacturing Corporation. Enter a 10-line adjusting journal directly in the connected spreadsheet, deliberately leaving it out of balance by one line, and observe how quickly the balancing-rule validation flags the problem back to you compared to the FBDI report-and-log review used earlier in this course.
slots.deliverable: One journal entered through Create Journal in Spreadsheet, first rejected in-session for an imbalance, then corrected and successfully uploaded.

slots.practicalActivity: Launch Create Invoice in Spreadsheet and enter 4 Payables invoices for LTV Manufacturing Corporation that arrived by email rather than a supplier-portal file -- the scale ADFdi is built for. Deliberately enter an invalid supplier site on one row, upload, read the in-session error ADFdi returns, and fix it without ever touching a CSV, ZIP, or UCM step.
slots.deliverable: 4 invoices entered and uploaded through Create Invoice in Spreadsheet, including one in-session error fixed on the spot.

lessons.title: Choosing FBDI vs. ADFdi vs. Manual Entry

slots.practicalActivity: Using this course's full decision framework (row volume, frequency, who's doing the work), write a one-paragraph recommendation for each of LTV Manufacturing Corporation's five Chapter 4 data-loading needs -- journals, Payables invoices, AutoInvoice receivables, Fixed Assets additions, and bank statements -- naming manual entry, FBDI, or ADFdi for each and justifying it against the real pipeline differences you hands-on tested earlier in this course.
slots.deliverable: A five-item written recommendation memo, one per Chapter 4 module, each justified against this course's decision framework and your own hands-on results.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can choose correctly among manual entry, FBDI, and ADFdi for a given Oracle Fusion data-loading need, and can build, run, monitor, troubleshoot, and correct real file-based imports and spreadsheet uploads for journals, Payables invoices, AutoInvoice receivables, Fixed Assets additions, bank statements, and suppliers.
